variants.headline: Foreign scrollwork sets the fashion in our streets
body: Shopkeepers here now copy a foreign fashion without being asked, and the clerks have raised the count to Influential at {{percentage}} percent. A cooper upriver carved strange scrollwork into a barrel head this week because a customer wanted it. Nobody in the shop could say where the pattern began.

variants.headline: In this year the voice of {{rival}} grew strong
body: The clerks of this year set the customs of {{rival}} at the Influential mark among our people, and their count was {{percentage}} percent. In the guild hall the apprentices now practise a border pattern before their masters will let them touch the old moulds.

variants.headline: What the children are singing
body: {{rival}} has climbed to Influential in our own streets, and we let it happen at the supper table. The children know a foreign verse from end to end before they know the songs of this town. Councilors, find one bench in this city where a local singer can earn a meal.

variants.headline: The teacher stops correcting the words
body: Behind the ropewalk the schoolmaster has given up marking the new song wrong; the pupils arrive knowing it whole. The foreign share of our habits now stands at {{percentage}} percent, which the clerks call Influential. Down at the gate a boy sells the words on a scrap of paper and cannot keep up with demand.

variants.headline: Our blue bolt sets the fashion across the border
body: A draper on the high street has ordered a second loom for the blue cloth that sells across the border. Our pull abroad has reached Influential at {{percentage}} percent. The carter on the north road leaves with a full bed and returns with a purse of orders.

variants.headline: Hear it! {{rival}} knows our jokes
body: {{terms.civic.people}}, listen! We hold the Influential mark in {{rival}}, and the count is {{percentage}} percent. Their players tell our jokes now, and their crowds laugh at the right moments. Our jokes, neighbors, coming home from across the border!

variants.headline: Our books could go farther through {{rival}}
body: Word from {{rival}} is that our influence there has reached Influential, with the count at {{percentage}} percent. A printer in that country who can fill a run may pay for translations, which would carry our writers into lands we never traded with. Booksellers past the next border may soon find our editions cheaper than fresh commissions.

variants.headline: Full houses, and the applause is sincere
body: A letter from a distant capital says our troupe fills the house there and turns latecomers away at the door. The clerks put our influence in that country at Influential. 'They do not clap out of politeness,' our correspondent writes. 'The last act earned it.'

variants.headline: The tailor clears his window: our pull slips to {{level}}
body: On the cobbled lane a tailor has taken down the foreign silks and hung his own cut in the window. The grip a rival people had on our taste has eased from {{previousLevel}} to {{level}}, down to {{percentage}} percent. Local cloth is moving again.

variants.headline: {{rival}} loses its grip on our tastes
body: Come spring, the guild school will open with a local ballad in place of the {{rival}} air it used to lead with. The hold of {{rival}} over our taste has softened from {{previousLevel}} to {{level}}. At the first rehearsal, half the hall will already be singing the replacement.

variants.headline: The market remembers its own
body: The hand of {{rival}} on our habits has slipped to {{level}}. At the market a potter has brought out her mother's clay cups again and swears she will throw another dozen if they sell. She asks the people at her stall what they want next. The big shops could learn from that.

variants.headline: In this year the foreign fashion faded
body: In this year the influence of a foreign people over our nation fell from {{previousLevel}} to {{level}}, as the clerks measured it. The elders say the young have gone back to the songs their grandmothers sang. What the town once borrowed, it is handing back.

variants.headline: Our cloth moves back as influence eases to {{level}}
body: Down at the export house a warehouseman has turned our bolt cloth to the back and put plainer goods in front. The tally of our standing there has slid from {{previousLevel}} to {{level}}, now at {{percentage}} percent. Next season's order book is thinner than this one.

variants.headline: Where our influence slipped in {{rival}}
body: Our influence in {{rival}} has dropped from {{previousLevel}} to {{level}}. A printer who once sent new plays across the border now keeps a shelf of unsold copies. The {{terms.civic.government}} should find out whether booksellers there stopped ordering or found a cheaper way to print their own.

variants.headline: Our fashions carry less weight in {{rival}}
body: Letters from {{rival}} tell us our cuts no longer rule the style there; a tailor of that capital, long known for copying our patterns, has put ours away. The clerks' tally records a fall there from {{previousLevel}} to {{level}}.

variants.headline: They've stopped singing our songs
body: A trader just in from the foreign port was asked if our songs still fill the streets over there. He paused. 'Every word is still in their mouths,' he said. 'They just no longer use them.' Our influence abroad has fallen to {{level}}.

variants.headline: Foreign influence over us turns {{trend}}
body: The pull of a rival nation on our people has turned {{trend}}, after a spell of running {{previousTrend}}. The tally is {{percentage}} percent, at the {{level}} grade. At the print shop the compositor gave the new number a larger face than the old, and the master let it stand.

variants.headline: Foreign influence has {{turnsToInfluential}} to Influential, a schoolmaster bets
body: A schoolmaster has ordered a second printing of the foreign songbook, betting the demand will outlast the term. The trend over us is now {{trend}}, and by the forecast it needs {{turnsToInfluential}} to reach Influential. If the bet fails, the spare copies will sit in his cupboard.

variants.headline: The cloth sellers knew before the scribes did
body: They say the cloth stalls have argued all season over the foreign bolt and the local weave, and the wives do not lower their voices. The scribes have finally sent their count, and the influence of {{rival}} over us has turned {{trend}}. The stalls claim they called it weeks ago.

variants.headline: The influence ledger
body: Hold of a foreign people on our taste: {{level}}
Share recorded at the last reckoning: {{percentage}} percent
Direction now: {{trend}}, previously {{previousTrend}}

variants.headline: Our influence abroad turns {{trend}}
body: Our reach over a rival people has swung {{trend}}, after a season of running {{previousTrend}}. The tally reads {{percentage}} percent, a grade of {{level}}. At the export house the clerk lays last season's order book beside the new one and traces both columns before naming a price.

variants.headline: Forecast: {{turnsToInfluential}} to Influential
body: Our standing abroad is {{trend}} tonight. Forecasters give us {{turnsToInfluential}} to reach Influential. At the export house, the shipping agent has set the autumn order sheet aside.

variants.headline: Our fashions rise again in {{rival}}
body: Letters from {{rival}} say our styles are back in favor at that court. A hostess of that capital is said to have blushed over the native wine she poured. The tally agrees, placing our influence at Rising and the {{level}} grade.

variants.headline: In this year our word carried less weight
body: It is recorded that our influence over {{rival}} swung to Falling in this year and now sits at the {{level}} grade. Fewer of their young came to study at our schools, the scribes observe. They wrote the change down as measured and added nothing.

variants.headline: Culture is a front line too
body: Our influence over a rival has swung {{trend}} and sits at the {{level}} grade. Border officers read that figure as a map. Where our songs are sung and our pots are sold, a patrol gets directions to the ford. Where neither is known, doors close and faces watch from the dark. A column crossing such a village loses a day before it ever finds the enemy.

variants.headline: {{city}} completes the {{wonder}} under an enemy flag
body: A shepherd on the border ridge saw the last scaffold come off the {{wonder}} above the walls of {{city}}. The work rose stone by stone while the fighting went on, and the fighting did not stop it.

variants.headline: An enemy city completes a wonder near our border
body: The {{wonder}} is done in an enemy city near our border. Travelers on the border road say the dust from the site settled only this week.

variants.headline: The {{wonder}} at {{city}} frees its masons for war
body: The {{wonder}} at {{city}} is done, and its masons are already asking where the next wages will come from. A country at war never lacks work for such hands. A crew that can lay a true course of stone can raise a rampart just as well. Where the enemy sends them next, a rampart will rise.

variants.headline: A fine hall under a hostile flag
body: This office has advice that the {{wonder}} in enemy {{city}} is finished, and that the stonework is very fine; our correspondent admits he lingered before it. The masons have earned their fee, whatever flag flies above them. It is a sad waste that such skill should serve a hostile sky.

variants.headline: The herd boys came back talking of towers
body: The boys came down from the pasture talking of towers across the line taller than ours. {{city}} had raised the {{wonder}}, they said, and they argued all the way home about what it was for. When enemy towers stand in view of the pasture, the war is the herders' too.

variants.headline: {{cityName}} completes the {{wonder}}
body: Builders in {{cityName}} have finished the {{wonder}}, and the city belongs to {{civilization}}. Scaffolds barely down, and travelers here are already asking the road to it.

variants.headline: A wonder finished abroad
body: A foreign city has just finished the {{wonder}}. By the time the report reached us the boards were down, and travelers here are already planning the detour.

variants.headline: The {{wonder}} makes {{civilization}} hard to forget
body: {{civilization}} has finished the {{wonder}}. A correspondent there reports that his editor wants yet another column about it. Our own planners might note how much room one work can win in papers that print that country's name only when its ministers make news.

variants.headline: They will walk you through every stone
body: Word is that the boards came off at {{cityName}} this season and left the {{wonder}} open to the sky. People who have seen it can talk of nothing else. Buy one of them a drink and every stone gets its own description.

variants.headline: The {{wonder}} at {{cityName}} is complete
body: Letters from {{cityName}} say the {{wonder}} is finished there, and the innkeepers report that visitors from many nations are already on the road, our own among them. Courts may quarrel, but a work of this order gives pleasure to every visitor who reaches it. May the crowds keep coming for many seasons.

variants.headline: A name for the histories is born in {{civilization}}
body: {{civilization}} has welcomed {{person}} into the world. Well-wishers filled the street before the evening meal, each carrying something small. A scribe arrived last and asked how the name was spelled.

variants.headline: A name for the histories is born
body: A new name, {{person}}, has entered the world, and no one yet agrees which court may claim them. Envoys from more than one court have knocked already, and the family keeps them waiting in the yard.

variants.headline: In this year a {{unit}} came to {{civilization}}
body: In this year {{civilization}} gained the {{unit}} {{person}}. The scribes entered the name in the margin as well as the line, a courtesy kept for no ordinary name.

variants.headline: A room is cleared before the work is chosen
body: {{person}} is ours. The works steward has orders to clear a room and find a bed by week's end, and no one has told him what the room is for. Art, state or war: the council has not chosen which. First the room gets its furniture; the purpose can wait.

variants.headline: Word for the {{terms.civic.people}}: a rival has a name we lack
body: Take note, {{terms.civic.people}}: {{civilization}} can name {{person}} as its own, and we cannot. Their gates have a fresh name to carve above them, and ours stand blank. Speak of friendship all you like; the ledger keeps no speeches.

variants.headline: The death of {{person}}
body: {{civilization}} rang its bells at noon for {{person}}, and the square had filled before the echoes died. That name was known far past the nation's borders. The news is on the road again tonight, in every direction.

variants.headline: The world is one name poorer
body: Death has taken {{person}}, and {{civilization}} has lost one of its own. While they lived, that name carried into many lands, and what they made survives where no flame can touch it. The shrine wardens have set a lamp beside the name and sworn to keep it burning until the season turns.

variants.headline: {{killer}} kills {{person}}
body: {{killer}} has killed {{person}} of {{civilization}}. The barracks heard before the family did, and the sergeant read the notice twice before he nailed it up. The yard went quiet.

variants.headline: They sat late at the fires tonight
body: Nobody moved from the fires tonight. {{person}}, one of our own, has died, and no one wanted to be the first away from the warmth. The stories began before the flames sank, and by morning each hearth will tell a different one.

variants.headline: Somebody sent {{person}} to their death
body: {{killer}} has taken {{person}} from us. Greatness does not stumble onto a battlefield; an order put one of our best within an enemy's reach, and that order has an author with a desk and a name. Give us the name. Let council hear those orders read out.

variants.headline: {{person}}'s study is cleared and the door locked
body: {{civilization}} has cleared the room where {{person}} worked and sent the books to the guild. The gift is spent, the work is done, and the key has been turned.

variants.headline: Notice: {{person}} spent in the nation's service
body: Let it be known that {{person}} has been spent in the nation's service. The council, in its customary foresight, turned the gift to a purpose of state. Not every detail is fit for the public eye. The public's thanks are owed all the same.

variants.headline: A talent spent is a bet on the present
body: Spending {{person}} turns a whole future into one act now, and {{civilization}} has made that bet on the present. Time and the account books will judge whether the bargain paid. Nobody thought to ask the person whose future it was.

variants.headline: The autograph he missed
body: In {{civilization}} a boy kept one blank page at the back of his copybook for {{person}} to sign. His father told him the work was finished before he had his chance. So he copied the name in his own hand. "Make the first letter big," he told his little sister.

variants.headline: New works on the walls of {{city}}
body: Crews in {{city}} have been up the ladders since first light, moving frames to make room. The count on the walls has grown by {{added}}, to {{total}} in all.

variants.headline: Notice to lovers of the arts
body: The galleries of {{city}} are richer by {{added|great work|great works}}, making {{total}} in all. They keep their usual hours. Linger as long as you please; the guards have been told to look the other way.

variants.headline: A neighboring gallery asks {{city}} for a winter loan
body: {{city}} has gained {{added|work|works}} for its collection, which now numbers {{total}}. The gallery in the next town has offered to send a wagon and fresh crates for a winter loan. Terms like those would carry art to towns that could never buy it.

variants.headline: The crates came up from the docks before dawn
body: Before dawn the crates were carried into the galleries of {{city}}, and by evening the gallery held {{added|new work|new works}}. The first admirers arrived by noon, and when the queue reached the fountain the guards stopped trying to move them along.

variants.headline: Great works lost from the galleries of {{city}}
body: The galleries of {{city}} hold {{lost}} fewer great works than at the last count, with {{total}} left. Twice a gallery hand has measured the empty spaces, then put his tape away without cutting a frame.

variants.headline: The walls of {{city}} are barer
body: The galleries of {{city}} held more in their best days. The walls have lost {{lost|great work|great works}}, and {{total}} still hang there. At closing the attendant makes his round, counting the hooks that hold nothing.

variants.headline: Print the names of the missing works
body: The count of great works in {{city}} has dropped by {{lost}}. If the works were carried off, the {{terms.civic.government}} should tell us where they stand now. If they have vanished, it should publish the names. One of our readers may know where a missing work has gone, if only we can tell her which one to look for.

variants.headline: The nail is still in the wall
body: The old keeper cannot bring himself to pull the nail where the painting hung. {{city}} has lost {{lost|great work|great works}} from its collection. The rest of the nation will hardly feel it. Here, every empty frame is felt.

variants.headline: The {{wonder}} stands at {{city}}
body: {{city}} has raised the {{wonder}} at last. A mason's wife brought her children to see what had kept him from supper all year, and the youngest stared a long time at the roof.

variants.headline: A wonder of our own is finished
body: The {{wonder}} is finished at last. The scaffolds have come down, and the first people through the gate this morning halted in the road to stare. One of them has already gone to fetch a neighbor.

variants.headline: Hear it, {{terms.civic.people}} of {{city}}! The {{wonder}} is done
body: The last plank is down! The {{wonder}} is done, and it belongs to us! Tell it at the well and at the gate: ours, ours! Let the neighbors walk over and see what our hands can raise, and carry the sight home with them!

variants.headline: The innkeeper at {{city}}'s {{wonder}} orders a second cart
body: An innkeeper outside the gate of {{city}} has ordered a second cart of ale for his yard. Visitors are already coming to look at the hall, and its masons have not yet left, their scaffolds stacked against the wall.

variants.headline: The children got there first
body: By evening the children of {{city}} had claimed the ground under the {{wonder}}, each one promising a taller one. The masons, their last plank down since noon, leaned on the fence and let them play.

variants.headline: The visitors come to {{civilization}} first
body: A guide in {{civilization}} now fills two walks a week, and the coach yard is turning carts away by noon. The tally now sets the country first at {{tourism}}, above the leader of last season.

variants.headline: A change at the top of the tourism table
body: A new name sits at the top of the visitors' table, with a rating of {{tourism}}. A guide with a folder of itineraries says customers now ask what they would see by taking a different road this year.

variants.headline: The tourism lead goes to {{civilization}}
body: Word reaches us that {{civilization}} stands alone at the head of the visitors' table, rated {{tourism}}. A travel almanac editor here plans to open his next edition with the country.

variants.headline: A share of first place for {{civilization}}
body: {{civilization}} now shares the top of the visitors' count at {{tourism}}. A booking clerk no longer calls the choice obvious.

variants.headline: Tourism: No. 1 for {{civilization}}
body: {{tourism}} on the visitors' table. First place.
